description: What each shipped saved search should return when the app is deployed against sample_events/. Generated numbers come from the same run_pipeline the determinism tests call; the expected-empty entries are stated with the reason, because a search returning nothing is the failure mode this whole app is careful about and it must be possible to tell a correct empty from a broken one.
corpus: tests/morpheus/determinism/telemetry_pipeline.py, lineage_pipeline.py and session_pipeline.py, rendered through SiemWireStage by make_sample_events.py

R-D-L2-001 - MAC address count exceeded.why: The rule joins port_designations, which ships header-only. Until an inventory populates it the lookup returns nothing and the join yields nothing. 11 candidate rows carry macs_per_port_first_in_window=true, so a non-zero result after populating the lookup is the signal that the join works.

R-D-L2-003 - ARP anomaly.why: The search aggregates BY arp_sender_ip, so the 24 contested observations collapse to one notable for the one address that is contested by two MACs.

R-D-L2-004 - MAC in two places at once.why: One address claimed on a peer switch inside a single poll sweep (conflict, zero gap) and one displaced two seconds later. Both are inside the 60-second threshold. The roaming device, displaced a whole poll cadence later, is deliberately outside it.

R-D-L2-005 - Authorization without authe.why: One authorization on a port whose own exchanges were long finished, and one that arrived while a legitimate exchange on its port was still open. The second only appears because exchanges are keyed by device; keyed by port it would have paired with the innocent device's request.

R-D-L5-003 - Impossible travel.why: One principal is authenticated from New York half an hour after her own office login in London, and then back in London ninety minutes later. Two rows rather than one is what a single interloper produces: the jump away and the victim's next authentication from where she actually is. The traveller who makes the same crossing in eight hours is inside the threshold and does not appear, and the VPN user whose apparent location changes country twice a day is excluded by egress range rather than alerted on.

R-D-L5-004 - Multi-factor fatigue.why: Five denials at ninety-second intervals and then an approval: six challenges inside eight minutes, which clears both thresholds. The fumbled password beside it -- two failed authentications and a success, with the factor never challenged -- is failure-then-success with none of the denial volume the rule requires, and does not appear.

R-C-002 - TLS anomaly precedes beaconing.why: A cross-layer rule needing layer 4 and layer 7 telemetry. Neither class exists in this fork, so no event can satisfy either half of the correlation. Empty here is correct and will stay correct until those classes ship.

Behavior summary - per-layer scores.why: Still empty, but no longer for the reason it was. `max_abs_z` now has a producer: TC5ScoreStage emits it on 105 of the 141 layer 5 events. What blocks this search is its grouping. It aggregates `by _time osi_layer entity_key lineage_id`, and no stage in this fork emits `osi_layer` at all while `entity_key` is present only on layer 1 -- so `stats by` drops every row. The envelope in Part 2 requires both on every record; the pipeline does not yet supply them. That is a gap in the producers rather than in this search.

Chain assembly - cross-layer risk.why: Aggregates across `osi_layer` and fires on a span of layers. Nothing emits `osi_layer`, so the grouping drops every row before the threshold is reached -- the same blocker as Behavior summary. Layer 5 now produces events, but from its own corpus and its own pipeline, so there is no chain spanning it and the layer 1 and 2 classes in any case.

Binding lookup - L2/L3 refresh.why: One row per key per five-minute bucket from binding_bucketed.jsonlines, written into the binding_l2_l3 KV Store collection. Every row carries binding_table=dhcp_lease, which is what the search filters on; a zero here means the producer stopped emitting that field and the lookup has quietly stopped being refreshed.

Binding lookup - L1 refresh.why: Five port intervals across four ports: three stable, and two on the port whose optic is swapped partway through the corpus. Produced by TC1BindingStage from the TC-1 stream. Note the lookup keys on port_id and switch_id with no bucket, so the two intervals on the swapped port collapse to one row and the later optic wins -- the lookup answers what is in a port now, not what was in it at a given time. See the open question recorded in Part 6 of the guide.

Binding lookup - L2/L3 expiry.why: A maintenance search that deletes buckets older than the retention window. On a freshly loaded corpus nothing is old enough to expire, so an empty result is the correct one.

Binding health - unresolved rate.why: One summary row over the ARP stream's resolution outcomes. This is an operational health metric rather than a detection, and it is the one search whose value is in the number rather than in whether it fired.
